[[File:Blechnum penna-marina Sheriff.jpg|thumb|Little Hard Fern near Mount Cook, New Zealand, November 2022]]

'''''Austroblechnum penna-marina''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Blechnum penna-marina''''',<ref name=CFLW_App>{{Citation |last1=Hassler |first1=Michael |last2=Schmitt |first2=Bernd |date=November 2019 |contribution=''Austroblechnum penna-marina'' ssp. ''penna-marina'' |title=Checklist of Ferns and Lycophytes of the World |at=8.11 |url=https://worldplants.webarchiv.kit.edu/ferns/ |access-date=2019-12-22 |name-list-style=amp |archive-date=2017-09-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170902225743/https://worldplants.webarchiv.kit.edu/ferns/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> known as '''Antarctic hard-fern''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''Little Hard Fern''', '''Alpine Hard Fern''', '''alpine water fern''' and '''pinque''' ([[Chilean Spanish]]), is a [[species]] of [[fern]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Blechnaceae. It is a widely distributed fern species in the [[Southern Hemisphere|southern hemisphere]], with a [[native plant|natural]] range including [[New Zealand]], [[Australia]], and [[South America]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last1=Brownsey |first1=P.J. |last2=Perrie |first2=L.R. |year=2021 |title=''Blechnum penna-marina'' (Poir.) Kuhn |url=https://www.nzflora.info/factsheet/taxon/Blechnum-penna-marina.html |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=NZFlora}}</ref>

It has wiry [[Rhizome|rhizomes]] and exhibits strong dimorphism in its [[Frond|fronds]].<ref name=":0" /> The sterile fronds are prostrate or semi-erect, growing up to 400 mm in length, while the fertile fronds are longer and held erect.<ref name=":0" /> The sterile fronds have a yellow-brown stem, while the fertile fronds have a purplish-black stipe. Both types of fronds have [[pinnatisect]] laminae with free veins.<ref name=":0" /> The sterile fronds have 12–44 pairs of triangular or oblong pinnae, while the fertile fronds have 10–36 pairs of linear to narrowly oblong pinnae, which are replaced by tiny sterile flanges at the base.<ref name=":0" />

This fern prefers coastal to alpine environments, including open forests, grasslands, subalpine scrub, alpine herb fields, creek beds, river terraces, and rocky herb fields.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=P. J. de. |year=2012 |title=Austroblechnum Penna-Marina Subsp. Alpina. |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/austroblechnum-penna-marina-subsp-alpina/ |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network}}</ref> It can be found from sea level up to 1900 meters above sea level.<ref name=":0" /> The preferred temperature range for its productivity is 6 to 11 degrees Celsius.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rossouw |first=M. W. |year=2016 |title=Functional response of ''Blechnum penna-marina'' to desiccation in tundra environments. |url=http://alp.lib.sun.ac.za/handle/123456789/28656 |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=Antarctic Legacy Archive}}</ref> It faces predation from endemic alpine grasshoppers such as ''[[Brachaspis nivalis]]'', ''[[Paprides nitidus]]'', and ''[[Sigaus australis]]''.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |year=2023 |title=''Blechnum penna-marina'' Host simple report |url=https://plant-synz.landcareresearch.co.nz/ReportForm.aspx?RecordId=All&Type=P&SortBy=Alpha |access-date=March 31, 2023 |website=PlantSynz - Invertebrate herbivore biodiversity assessment tool: Database |publisher=Landcare Research}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
French botanist [[Jean Louis Marie Poiret]] first described this species as ''Polypodium penna-marina'' in 1804 in “[[Encyclopédie_Méthodique|Encyclopédie Méthodique Botanique]]”, and it was later shifted to ''Blechnum penna-marina'' by German botanist [[Friedrich Adalbert Maximilian Kuhn]] in 1868.<ref name=":0" /> In 2016 it was placed in the new genus ''Austroblechnum'', as ''Austroblechnum penna-marina'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Gasper |first1=André Luís De |last2=Dittrich |first2=Vinícius Antonio De Oliveira |last3=Smith |first3=Alan Reid |last4=Salino |first4=Alexandre |title=A classification for Blechnaceae (Polypodiales: Polypodiopsida): New genera, resurrected names, and combinations |journal=Phytotaxa |date=2016 |volume=275 |issue=3 |pages=191–227 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.275.3.1 |url=https://doi.org/10.11646/phytotaxa.275.3.1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> although this change has not been widely used.

The species name "penna-marina" refers to its feather-like appearance and its coastal habitat.<ref name=":0" />

== Description ==

=== Appearance ===

''Blechnum penna-marina'' features a wiry rhizome, which gives rise to long creeping and sparing branches.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Allan |first1=H. H. |last2=Farrant |first2=P. A. |last3=Chambers |first3=T. C. |date=17 September 2020 |title=''Blechnum penna-marina'' |url=https://biotanz.landcareresearch.co.nz/scientific-names/9369ee73-d7f0-4f04-9e10-f1adc476a172 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518081844/https://biotanz.landcareresearch.co.nz/scientific-names/9369ee73-d7f0-4f04-9e10-f1adc476a172 |archive-date=18 May 2023 |access-date=29 March 2023 |website=Biota of New Zealand |publisher=New Zealand Landcare Research}}</ref> The fronds of this species exhibit strong dimorphism, with sterile fronds growing up to 400 mm when semi-erect in manner, while fertile fronds are longer and held erect, often reaching twice the length of the sterile fronds.<ref name=":0" /> Sterile fronds have a yellow-brown stem, whereas fertile fronds have a purplish-black stipe. The laminae of both sterile and fertile fronds are [[pinnatisect]], linear to narrowly elliptic, tapering to a pinnatifid apex, and [[Glossary of botanical terms|coriaceous]], with free veins.<ref name=":0" /> The sterile fronds bear 12–44 pairs of triangular or oblong pinnae, while the fertile fronds have 10–36 pairs of linear to narrowly oblong pinnae, which are replaced by tiny sterile flanges at the base of the lamina.<ref name=":0" />

=== Size ===
The varying sizes of the fronds contribute to the distinct appearance of ''Blechnum penna-marina'', with the sterile fronds being shorter and the fertile fronds being taller and more upright.<ref name=":0" /> The size difference between the two types of fronds is an important characteristic to differentiate this species and adds to its overall aesthetic appeal.

The sterile fronds of this species typically grow to a length of 15–400 mm in a prostrate or semi-erect manner.<ref name=":0" /> Fertile fronds are longer and held erect, often reaching up to twice the length of the sterile fronds.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==
The species is widely distributed throughout the global south, including New Zealand, Australia, and South America.<ref name=":0" /> It is native to [[Marion Island]], a subantarctic island halfway between Africa and Antarctica.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chau |first1=John H. |last2=Mtsi |first2=Nasipi I. S. |last3=Münbergová |first3=Zuzana |last4=Greve |first4=Michelle |last5=le Roux |first5=Peter C. |last6=Mairal |first6=Mario |last7=Le Roux |first7=Johannes J. |last8=Dorrington |first8=Rosemary A. |last9=Jansen van Vuuren |first9=Bettine |date=November 2020 |title=An update on the indigenous vascular flora of sub-Antarctic Marion Island: taxonomic changes, sequences for DNA barcode loci, and genome size data |journal=Polar Biology |volume=43 |issue=11 |pages=1817–1828 |doi=10.1007/s00300-020-02747-7 |url=https://mariomairal.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Chau2020_Article_AnUpdateOnTheIndigenousVascula-1.pdf  |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231112020200/https://mariomairal.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/Chau2020_Article_AnUpdateOnTheIndigenousVascula-1.pdf |archive-date=12 November 2023 |access-date=2 July 2025}}</ref>

Within New Zealand, this fern species can be found throughout the country, spanning from the [[North Island]] to the [[South Island]], including the [[Chatham Islands|Chatham]], [[Stewart Island|Stewart]], [[Auckland Islands|Auckland]], [[Campbell Island, New Zealand|Campbell]], and [[Antipodes Islands]].<ref name=":0" /> It exhibits a broad altitudinal range, from sea level up to 1900 meters above sea level.<ref name=":0" /> In the North Island, ''Blechnum penna-marina'' is found in the lowlands to alpine regions, extending from [[Hamilton, New Zealand|Hamilton]] and [[East Cape]] to [[Newtown, New Zealand|south Wellington]].<ref name=":0" /> Similarly, in the South Island and Stewart Island, it occurs in the lowland to alpine areas.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Notably, it has been observed growing at high elevations of up to 1900 meters above sea level in the [[Spenser Mountains]], Nelson.<ref name=":0" /> The wide geographic distribution of ''Blechnum penna-marina'' highlights its adaptability to diverse habitats and climates across the southern hemisphere.<ref name=":0" />

== Interactions ==
[[File:Blechnum penna-marina Sullivan.jpg|thumb|Pinnae of ''Blechnum penna-marina'']]
There are few identified enemies of ''Blechnum penna-marina.'' ''Blechnum penna-marina'' is subject to herbivory by several endemic grasshopper species in New Zealand. The grasshoppers ''[[Brachaspis nivalis]]'', ''[[Paprides nitidus]]'', and ''[[Sigaus australis]]'' are known to feed on the pinnae of ''Blechnum penna-marina''.<ref name=":2" /> These grasshoppers inhabit areas with vegetation covering the ground and can be found in alpine environments where Little Hard Fern grows well.<ref name=":2" /> While these grasshoppers are considered endemic to New Zealand, their presence indicates a potential interaction between the fern and native herbivores in other ecosystems.<ref name=":2" /> The impact of these grasshoppers on the population dynamics and growth of ''Blechnum penna-marina'' warrants further investigation, as it may play a role in shaping the fern's distribution and abundance in its natural habitat.

No fungal parasites or diseases have been recorded for this species as of March 30, 2023.<ref name=":2" />
